decisions.choice: single quotation marks inside the story
decisions.reason: The whole story is told by Jesus, so the words of the people in it are a quotation inside his speech.

decisions.choice: plural_you spans on the words addressed to the workers ({{plural_you:Vayan|Id}}, {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, {{plural_you:les|os}})
decisions.reason: Spanish has two plural forms of "you", Latin American "ustedes" and Peninsular "vosotros"; the setting chooses between them. English has no such choice, so these spans have no English counterpart. The same throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: the owner says "tôi" and calls the laborers "các anh"; they call him "ông" (20:4-15)
decisions.reason: An employer hiring free laborers speaks to them politely; unlike the king of 18:32, he is not rebuking a servant.

decisions.choice: The owner speaks to the laborers in 해라체, and they answer him in 합쇼체, through the parable; single quotation marks inside the story
decisions.reason: A landowner speaking to day laborers he hires; the laborers address their employer deferentially. Quotations inside Jesus's story take single marks, as in the English.

decisions.choice: “ ” for the speakers inside the parable
decisions.reason: The parable is already inside Jesus's words, which open with « » earlier in his speech, so the owner's and workers' words take the inner marks, as the English uses single marks.

decisions.choice: 『』 for the words of people in the story; the owner speaks to the laborers plainly, they answer him politely (20:7, 12)
decisions.reason: The story is told by Jesus, so the speech inside it is a quotation within his speech (r-en-2). An employer speaks to day laborers in the plain style, and they answer with です・ます.

ja.L: そこで彼らは出かけて行った。
ja.B: そこで彼らは出かけて行った。
ja.R: それで、その人たちは出かけて行った。

decisions.choice: they went: they took the work without a set wage
decisions.reason: They went into the vineyard on the owner's word alone.

source.text: πάλιν ἐξελθὼν περὶ ἕκτην καὶ ἐνάτην ὥραν ἐποίησεν ὡσαύτως.

records.literal_gloss: Again having gone out about [the] sixth and ninth hour he did likewise.

en.L: Again, going out about the sixth and the ninth hour, he did likewise.
en.B: He went out again around noon, and again around three in the afternoon, and did the same.
en.R: He went out again at about twelve noon and at about three in the afternoon. Each time he did the same thing.

es.L: Saliendo otra vez hacia la hora sexta y [la] novena, hizo lo mismo.
es.B: Volvió a salir hacia el mediodía, y otra vez hacia las tres de la tarde, e hizo lo mismo.
es.R: Salió otra vez como a las doce del mediodía y como a las tres de la tarde. Cada vez hizo lo mismo.

fr.L: Étant sorti de nouveau vers la sixième et la neuvième heure, il a fait de même.
fr.B: Il est ressorti vers midi, puis vers quinze heures, et il a fait de même.
fr.R: Il est ressorti vers midi, et encore vers trois heures de l’après-midi. Chaque fois, il a fait la même chose.

sw.L: Tena, alipotoka yapata saa sita na saa tisa, alifanya vivyo hivyo.
sw.B: Alitoka tena karibu saa sita mchana, na tena karibu saa tisa, akafanya vivyo hivyo.
sw.R: Alitoka tena yapata saa sita mchana na saa tisa alasiri. Kila mara alifanya vilevile.

vi.L: Khoảng giờ thứ sáu và giờ thứ chín, ông lại đi ra và cũng làm như vậy.
vi.B: Khoảng giữa trưa và khoảng ba giờ chiều, ông lại ra ngoài và cũng làm như thế.
vi.R: Khoảng mười hai giờ trưa và khoảng ba giờ chiều, ông lại ra ngoài. Mỗi lần ông đều làm như vậy.

ko.L: 다시 여섯째 시와 아홉째 시쯤에 나가서, 그와 같이 하였다.
ko.B: 그는 낮 열두 시쯤과 오후 세 시쯤에도 다시 나가서 그렇게 했다.
ko.R: 그는 낮 열두 시쯤에 다시 나갔다. 오후 세 시쯤에도 나갔다. 그리고 그때마다 똑같이 일꾼들을 데려왔다.

pt.L: De novo, saindo por volta da hora sexta e da hora nona, fez do mesmo modo.
pt.B: Ele saiu de novo por volta do meio-dia e outra vez por volta das três da tarde, e fez o mesmo.
pt.R: Ele saiu outra vez por volta do meio-dia e depois por volta das três horas da tarde. Nas duas vezes, fez a mesma coisa.

am.L: ደግሞም በስድስተኛውና በዘጠነኛው ሰዓት ገደማ ወጥቶ እንዲሁ አደረገ።
am.B: እኩለ ቀን ገደማ እንደገና ወጣ፤ ከቀኑ ዘጠኝ ሰዓት ገደማም ወጣ፤ እንደዚያውም አደረገ።
am.R: እኩለ ቀን ገደማና ከቀኑ ዘጠኝ ሰዓት ገደማ እንደገና ወጣ። በየጊዜውም እንደዚያው አደረገ።

ru.L: Снова выйдя около шестого и девятого часа, он сделал так же.
ru.B: Около полудня он вышел снова, и ещё раз около трёх часов дня, и сделал то же самое.
ru.R: Он выходил снова около двенадцати часов дня и около трёх часов дня. И каждый раз делал то же самое.

hi.L: फिर छठे और नौवें घंटे के लगभग निकलकर उसने वैसा ही किया।
hi.B: वह फिर दोपहर लगभग बारह बजे और फिर लगभग तीन बजे निकला और उसने वैसा ही किया।
hi.R: वह दोपहर लगभग बारह बजे फिर बाहर गया, और फिर लगभग तीन बजे भी। हर बार उसने वैसा ही किया।

uk.L: Знову, вийшовши близько шостої і девʼятої години, зробив так само.
uk.B: Він виходив знову близько полудня й ще раз близько третьої по обіді, і робив так само.
uk.R: Він знову вийшов близько дванадцятої години дня і близько третьої години по обіді. Щоразу він робив те саме.

ja.L: 再び、第六の時と第九の時ごろに出て行って、同じようにした。
ja.B: その人は正午ごろにも、また午後三時ごろにも出て行って、同じようにした。
ja.R: その人は、昼の十二時ごろと午後三時ごろにも出かけて行った。そして、そのたびに同じようにした。

decisions.choice: the sixth and ninth hour: about noon and about three in the afternoon
decisions.reason: Counting from sunrise, the sixth hour was midday and the ninth was the middle of the afternoon.

decisions.choice: likewise: he hired more workers on the same terms
decisions.reason: He did as at the third hour, sending them in with a promise of what is fair.

decisions.choice: noon; three in the afternoon
alternatives: the sixth and the ninth hour
decisions.reason: The day was counted from sunrise, about six in the morning, in twelve hours (John 11:9). Balanced and Readable give the time as a modern reader tells it; Literal keeps the hour as the Greek counts it.

decisions.choice: quinze heures (B); trois heures de l’après-midi (R)
alternatives: trois heures de l’après-midi at Balanced
decisions.reason: As Mark 15:33: written French gives the afternoon hour on the 24-hour clock; Readable says it as people say it aloud. The same in 20:6 and 20:9.

source.text: περὶ δὲ τὴν ἑνδεκάτην ἐξελθὼν εὗρεν ἄλλους ἑστῶτας, καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Τί ὧδε ἑστήκατε ὅλην τὴν ἡμέραν ἀργοί;

records.literal_gloss: About then the eleventh having gone out he found others standing, and he says to them, Why here have you stood all the day idle?

en.L: And going out about the eleventh [hour], he found others standing, and he says to them, 'Why have you been standing here idle the whole day?'
en.B: Then, about five in the afternoon, he went out and found still others standing there. 'Why have you been standing here all day doing nothing?' he asked them.
en.R: At about five o'clock in the afternoon, he went out again and found more people standing there. He asked them, 'Why have you been standing here all day without working?'

es.L: Y saliendo hacia la undécima [hora], encontró a otros que estaban allí, y les dice: “¿Por qué {{plural_you:han estado|habéis estado}} aquí todo el día sin trabajo?”.
es.B: Luego, hacia las cinco de la tarde, salió y encontró a otros que seguían allí. “¿Por qué {{plural_you:han estado|habéis estado}} aquí todo el día sin hacer nada?”, les preguntó.
es.R: Como a las cinco de la tarde salió otra vez y encontró a más personas que estaban allí. Les preguntó: “¿Por qué {{plural_you:han estado|habéis estado}} aquí todo el día sin trabajar?”.

fr.L: Et vers la onzième, étant sorti, il en a trouvé d’autres qui se tenaient là, et il leur dit : “Pourquoi vous tenez-vous ici toute la journée sans rien faire ?”
fr.B: Puis, vers dix-sept heures, il est sorti et en a trouvé encore d’autres qui étaient là. Il leur a demandé : “Pourquoi êtes-vous restés ici toute la journée sans rien faire ?”
fr.R: Vers cinq heures de l’après-midi, il est encore sorti et il a trouvé d’autres gens qui attendaient là. Il leur a demandé : “Pourquoi êtes-vous restés ici toute la journée sans travailler ?”

sw.L: Na alipotoka yapata saa kumi na moja, aliwaona wengine wamesimama, naye anawaambia, 'Kwa nini mmesimama hapa siku nzima bila kazi?'
sw.B: Kisha karibu saa kumi na moja jioni alitoka, akawakuta wengine bado wamesimama pale. Akawauliza, 'Kwa nini mmesimama hapa siku nzima bila kufanya kitu?'
sw.R: Yapata saa kumi na moja jioni alitoka tena, akawakuta watu wengine wamesimama pale. Akawauliza, 'Kwa nini mmesimama hapa siku nzima bila kufanya kazi?'

vi.L: Khoảng giờ thứ mười một, ông đi ra và thấy những người khác đứng đó, và ông nói với họ: 'Sao các anh đứng không ở đây cả ngày?'
vi.B: Rồi khoảng năm giờ chiều, ông ra ngoài và thấy vẫn còn những người khác đứng đó. Ông hỏi họ: 'Sao các anh đứng đây cả ngày mà không làm gì cả?'
vi.R: Khoảng năm giờ chiều, ông lại ra ngoài và thấy có thêm mấy người đang đứng đó. Ông hỏi họ: 'Sao các anh đứng đây cả ngày mà không làm việc?'

ko.L: 그리고 열한째 [시]쯤에 나가서, 다른 사람들이 서 있는 것을 보고 그들에게 말한다. '왜 너희는 온종일 하는 일 없이 여기 서 있느냐?'
ko.B: 오후 다섯 시쯤에 그가 또 나가 보니, 아직도 다른 사람들이 서 있었다. 그가 그들에게 물었다. '왜 하루 종일 일도 안 하고 여기 서 있느냐?'
ko.R: 오후 다섯 시쯤에 그는 또 나갔다. 그런데 거기 또 다른 사람들이 서 있었다. 그는 그들에게 물었다. '너희는 왜 하루 종일 일하지 않고 여기 서 있느냐?'

pt.L: E, saindo por volta da [hora] décima primeira, encontrou outros parados, e lhes diz: 'Por que vocês estão parados aqui o dia inteiro, desocupados?'
pt.B: Depois, por volta das cinco da tarde, ele saiu e encontrou ainda outros parados ali. 'Por que vocês ficaram aqui o dia todo sem fazer nada?', perguntou a eles.
pt.R: Por volta das cinco horas da tarde, ele saiu outra vez e encontrou mais pessoas paradas ali. Ele perguntou a elas: 'Por que vocês ficaram aqui parados o dia inteiro sem trabalhar?'

am.L: በአሥራ አንደኛውም [ሰዓት] ገደማ ወጥቶ ሌሎች ቆመው አገኘ፤ እንዲህም ይላቸዋል፦ “ቀኑን ሙሉ ሥራ ፈትታችሁ ለምን እዚህ ቆማችኋል?”
am.B: ከዚያም ከቀኑ አሥራ አንድ ሰዓት ገደማ ወጥቶ ሌሎች ሰዎች በዚያ ቆመው አገኘ። “ቀኑን ሙሉ ምንም ሳትሠሩ ለምን እዚህ ቆማችኋል?” ሲል ጠየቃቸው።
am.R: ከቀኑ አሥራ አንድ ሰዓት ገደማ እንደገና ወጥቶ ሌሎች ሰዎች በዚያ ቆመው አገኘ። እርሱም “ቀኑን ሙሉ ሳትሠሩ ለምን እዚህ ቆማችኋል?” ብሎ ጠየቃቸው።

ru.L: Около же одиннадцатого [часа] выйдя, он нашёл других стоящих и говорит им: “Почему вы здесь стоите весь день без дела?”
ru.B: А около пяти часов вечера он вышел и нашёл ещё других, стоявших там. “Почему вы стоите здесь весь день и ничего не делаете?” — спросил он их.
ru.R: Около пяти часов вечера он вышел опять и нашёл там ещё людей. Он спросил их: “Почему вы стоите здесь весь день и не работаете?”

hi.L: और ग्यारहवें [घंटे] के लगभग निकलकर उसने दूसरों को खड़े पाया, और वह उनसे कहता है, 'तुम यहाँ सारा दिन बेकार क्यों खड़े रहे हो?'
hi.B: फिर शाम के लगभग पाँच बजे वह निकला और उसने कुछ और लोगों को वहाँ खड़े पाया। 'तुम यहाँ सारा दिन बिना काम के क्यों खड़े हो?' उसने उनसे पूछा।
hi.R: शाम के लगभग पाँच बजे वह फिर निकला और उसे कुछ और लोग वहाँ खड़े मिले। उसने उनसे पूछा, 'तुम सारा दिन यहाँ बिना काम के क्यों खड़े हो?'

uk.L: Вийшовши ж близько одинадцятої, він знайшов інших, що стояли, і каже їм: “Чому ви стоїте тут увесь день без діла?”
uk.B: Потім, близько пʼятої по обіді, він вийшов і знайшов там ще інших. “Чому ви стоїте тут цілий день і нічого не робите?” — запитав він їх.
uk.R: Близько пʼятої години по обіді він знову вийшов і знайшов там ще людей. Він запитав їх: “Чому ви стоїте тут увесь день і не працюєте?”

ja.L: また、第十一[の時]ごろに出て行って、ほかの人々が立っているのを見つけた。そして彼らに言う。『なぜ、一日中何もしないで、ここに立っているのか？』
ja.B: それから午後五時ごろに出て行くと、まだほかの人々が立っていた。『なぜ一日中何もしないで、ここに立っているのか？』とその人は彼らに尋ねた。
ja.R: 夕方の五時ごろにも、その人は出かけて行った。すると、またほかの人たちが立っていた。その人は聞いた。『なぜ一日中、働かないでここに立っているのか？』

decisions.choice: the eleventh hour: about five in the afternoon, one hour before work ended
decisions.reason: The eleventh hour was about an hour before sunset. The other workers say these men worked only one hour (20:12).

decisions.choice: the eleventh, without "hour"; standing, without "idle"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "hour" after "the eleventh" and "idle" after "standing", which say the same thing more fully. The SBLGNT follows earlier manuscripts that lack both. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: five in the afternoon (B); five o'clock in the afternoon (R)
decisions.reason: The day was counted from sunrise, about six in the morning, in twelve hours (John 11:9). Balanced and Readable give the time as a modern reader tells it; Literal keeps the hour as the Greek counts it.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: historic present at Literal (les dice); past at Balanced and Readable (les preguntó)
decisions.reason: Matthew tells parts of the story in the present (English decision r-en-2). Literal keeps it, as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable tell the story in the past, as Spanish narrative does. The same in verses 7 and 8.

decisions.choice: historic present kept at Literal (anawaambia); past at Balanced and Readable (akawauliza)
decisions.reason: Matthew tells parts of the story in the present (English decision r-en-2). Literal keeps it, as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable tell the story in the narrative past, with -li- for the first verb and -ka- for those that follow. The same in verses 7 and 8.

decisions.choice: "nói" with no "đã" (L) for the historic present, also 20:7-8
decisions.reason: As elsewhere in Matthew, Literal keeps the present by leaving out "đã".

decisions.choice: [시]; present "말한다" (L)
decisions.reason: The Greek says "the eleventh" without "hour" (meaning decision); Literal brackets the word Korean needs, and keeps Matthew's present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: present "言う" (L, and in 20:7, 8); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps Matthew's present tense of narration, as the English Literal does and as in 9:28; Balanced and Readable tell the story in the past.

source.text: λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Ὅτι οὐδεὶς ἡμᾶς ἐμισθώσατο.

records.literal_gloss: They say to him, Because no one us has hired.

en.L: They say to him, 'Because no one has hired us.'
en.B: 'Because nobody has hired us,' they answered.
en.R: They answered, 'No one has hired us.'

es.L: Le dicen: “Porque nadie nos ha contratado”.
es.B: “Porque nadie nos ha contratado”, le respondieron.
es.R: Ellos le respondieron: “Nadie nos ha dado trabajo”.

fr.L: Ils lui disent : “Parce que personne ne nous a embauchés.”
fr.B: Ils lui ont répondu : “Parce que personne ne nous a embauchés.”
fr.R: Ils ont répondu : “Personne ne nous a engagés.”

sw.B: Wakamjibu, 'Ni kwa sababu hakuna aliyetupa kazi.'

vi.L: Họ nói với ông: 'Vì không ai mướn chúng tôi.'
vi.B: Họ đáp: 'Vì không có ai mướn chúng tôi cả.'
vi.R: Họ trả lời: 'Không có ai mướn chúng tôi.'

ko.L: 그들이 그에게 말한다. '아무도 저희를 고용하지 않았기 때문입니다.'
ko.B: 그들이 대답했다. '아무도 저희에게 일을 시켜 주지 않았기 때문입니다.'
ko.R: 그들이 대답했다. '아무도 저희를 써 주지 않았습니다.'

pt.L: Eles lhe dizem: 'Porque ninguém nos contratou.'

ru.L: Говорят ему: “Потому что никто нас не нанял.”
ru.B: “Потому что никто нас не нанял”, — ответили они.

hi.L: वे उससे कहते हैं, 'क्योंकि किसी ने हमें मज़दूरी पर नहीं लगाया।'
hi.B: 'क्योंकि किसी ने हमें काम पर नहीं रखा,' उन्होंने उत्तर दिया।
hi.R: उन्होंने जवाब दिया, 'किसी ने हमें काम पर नहीं रखा।'

uk.L: Кажуть йому: “Бо ніхто нас не найняв.”
uk.B: “Бо ніхто нас не найняв”, — відповіли вони.

ja.L: 彼らはその人に言う。『だれもわたしたちを雇ってくれないからです。』
ja.B: 『だれも雇ってくれないからです』と彼らは答えた。
ja.R: その人たちは答えた。『だれも雇ってくれないのです。』

decisions.choice: because no one has hired us: they wanted work but found none
decisions.reason: Their answer explains why they are idle. The owner takes them at their word.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

source.text: λέγει αὐτοῖς· Ὑπάγετε καὶ ὑμεῖς εἰς τὸν ἀμπελῶνα.

records.literal_gloss: He says to them, Go also you into the vineyard.

en.L: He says to them, 'You also go into the vineyard.'
en.B: He told them, 'You go to the vineyard too.'
en.R: He told them, 'Then you can go and work in my vineyard too.'

es.L: Les dice: “{{plural_you:Vayan|Id}} también {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} a la viña”.
es.B: Él les dijo: “{{plural_you:Vayan|Id}} {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} también a la viña”.
es.R: Entonces les dijo: “Pues {{plural_you:pueden|podéis}} ir {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} también a trabajar en mi viña”.

fr.L: Il leur dit : “Allez, vous aussi, dans la vigne.”
fr.B: Il leur a dit : “Allez, vous aussi, à la vigne.”
fr.R: Il leur a dit : “Alors, vous aussi, vous pouvez aller travailler dans ma vigne.”

sw.L: Anawaambia, 'Ninyi pia nendeni kwenye shamba la mizabibu.'
sw.B: Akawaambia, 'Nendeni nanyi kwenye shamba la mizabibu.'
sw.R: Akawaambia, 'Basi, nanyi mnaweza kwenda kufanya kazi katika shamba langu la mizabibu.'

vi.L: Ông nói với họ: 'Các anh cũng hãy vào vườn nho.'
vi.B: Ông bảo họ: 'Các anh cũng hãy vào làm vườn nho đi.'
vi.R: Ông bảo họ: 'Vậy các anh cũng hãy vào làm việc trong vườn nho của tôi.'

ko.B: 그가 그들에게 말했다. '너희도 포도원에 가서 일하여라.'
ko.R: 그가 그들에게 말했다. '그러면 너희도 내 포도원에 가서 일해라.'

pt.L: Ele lhes diz: 'Vão também vocês para a vinha.'
pt.B: Ele lhes disse: 'Vão vocês também para a vinha.'
pt.R: Ele disse a eles: 'Então vocês também podem ir trabalhar na minha vinha.'

am.L: ይላቸዋል፦ “እናንተም ደግሞ ወደ ወይን ቦታው ሂዱ።”
am.R: እርሱም “እንግዲያውስ እናንተም ሄዳችሁ በወይን ቦታዬ ሥሩ” አላቸው።

ru.L: Говорит им: “Идите и вы в виноградник.”
ru.B: Он сказал им: “Идите и вы в виноградник.”
ru.R: Он сказал им: “Тогда и вы можете пойти работать в мой виноградник.”

hi.L: वह उनसे कहता है, 'तुम भी दाख की बारी में जाओ।'
hi.B: उसने उनसे कहा, 'तुम भी दाख की बारी में चले जाओ।'
hi.R: उसने उनसे कहा, 'तो तुम भी जाकर मेरे बाग़ में काम करो।'

uk.L: Каже їм: “Ідіть і ви до виноградника.”
uk.B: Він сказав їм: “Ідіть і ви до виноградника.”
uk.R: Він сказав їм: “Тоді ви теж можете піти працювати в моєму винограднику.”

ja.L: [その人は]彼らに言う。『あなたがたもぶどう園に行きなさい。』
ja.B: その人は言った。『あなたがたもぶどう園へ行きなさい。』
ja.R: その人は言った。『それなら、あなたたちも、わたしのぶどう園に行って働きなさい。』

decisions.choice: the SBLGNT ends with the vineyard; no wage is promised
alternatives: adds: and whatever is right you will receive
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "and whatever is right you will receive", repeating 20:4. Earlier manuscripts lack it. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: go and work in my vineyard
decisions.reason: As in 20:4, Readable says why they go.

source.text: ὀψίας δὲ γενομένης λέγει ὁ κύριος τοῦ ἀμπελῶνος τῷ ἐπιτρόπῳ αὐτοῦ· Κάλεσον τοὺς ἐργάτας καὶ ἀπόδος αὐτοῖς τὸν μισθὸν ἀρξάμενος ἀπὸ τῶν ἐσχάτων ἕως τῶν πρώτων.

records.literal_gloss: Evening then having come says the master of the vineyard to the foreman of him, Call the workmen and pay them the wages, having begun from the last unto the first.

en.L: And when evening had come, the master of the vineyard says to his foreman, 'Call the workers and pay them the wages, beginning from the last up to the first.'
en.B: When evening came, the owner of the vineyard told his manager, 'Call in the laborers and give them their pay. Start with the ones hired last and finish with the first.'
en.R: When evening came, the owner of the vineyard spoke to the man in charge of his workers. He said, 'Call the workers and pay them. Begin with the people I hired last, and end with the ones I hired first.'

es.L: Y al caer la tarde, dice el señor de la viña a su encargado: “Llama a los trabajadores y entrégales el salario, empezando por los últimos hasta los primeros”.
es.B: Al caer la tarde, el dueño de la viña le dijo a su encargado: “Llama a los jornaleros y págales lo que les corresponde. Empieza por los últimos que llegaron y termina con los primeros”.
es.R: Cuando llegó la tarde, el dueño de la viña habló con el hombre que estaba a cargo de sus trabajadores. Le dijo: “Llama a los trabajadores y págales. Empieza por los que contraté al final y termina con los que contraté primero”.

fr.L: Et le soir venu, le maître de la vigne dit à son intendant : “Appelle les ouvriers et paie-leur le salaire, en commençant par les derniers jusqu’aux premiers.”
fr.B: Le soir venu, le propriétaire de la vigne a dit à son intendant : “Fais venir les ouvriers et donne-leur leur salaire. Commence par ceux qui ont été embauchés en dernier et finis par les premiers.”
fr.R: Quand le soir est arrivé, le propriétaire de la vigne a parlé à l’homme qui dirigeait ses ouvriers. Il lui a dit : “Appelle les ouvriers et paie-les. Commence par ceux que j’ai engagés en dernier, et termine par ceux que j’ai engagés en premier.”

sw.L: Na jioni ilipoingia, bwana wa shamba la mizabibu anamwambia msimamizi wake, 'Waite vibarua uwape malipo yao, ukianza na wale wa mwisho mpaka wale wa kwanza.'
sw.B: Jioni ilipofika, mwenye shamba la mizabibu alimwambia msimamizi wake, 'Waite vibarua uwape malipo yao. Anza na walioajiriwa mwisho, umalizie na wa kwanza.'
sw.R: Jioni ilipofika, mwenye shamba la mizabibu alizungumza na mtu aliyesimamia wafanyakazi wake. Akamwambia, 'Waite wafanyakazi uwalipe. Anza na wale niliowaajiri mwisho, umalizie na wale niliowaajiri kwanza.'

vi.L: Khi chiều đến, chủ vườn nho nói với người quản lý của mình: 'Hãy gọi những người thợ và trả tiền công cho họ, bắt đầu từ những người sau cùng cho đến những người đầu tiên.'
vi.B: Đến chiều, chủ vườn nho bảo người quản lý: 'Hãy gọi những người làm công lại và trả công cho họ. Bắt đầu từ những người đến sau cùng, rồi đến những người đến trước nhất.'
vi.R: Đến chiều, chủ vườn nho nói với người trông coi những người làm công: 'Hãy gọi những người làm công lại và trả tiền cho họ. Bắt đầu với những người tôi mướn sau cùng, và kết thúc với những người tôi mướn trước hết.'

ko.L: 저녁이 되자, 포도원 주인이 자기 관리인에게 말한다. '일꾼들을 불러 품삯을 주어라. 마지막 사람들부터 시작하여 처음 사람들까지 [주어라].'
ko.B: 저녁이 되자 포도원 주인이 관리인에게 말했다. '일꾼들을 불러 품삯을 주어라. 맨 나중에 온 사람들부터 시작해서 맨 먼저 온 사람들까지 주어라.'
ko.R: 저녁이 되자 포도원 주인은 일꾼들을 맡아 관리하는 사람에게 말했다. '일꾼들을 불러서 품삯을 주어라. 내가 맨 나중에 데려온 사람들부터 주고, 맨 처음 데려온 사람들에게 마지막으로 주어라.'

pt.L: E, chegada a tarde, o senhor da vinha diz ao seu administrador: 'Chame os trabalhadores e pague a eles o salário, começando pelos últimos até os primeiros.'
pt.B: Ao cair da tarde, o dono da vinha disse ao seu administrador: 'Chame os trabalhadores e pague a eles o que lhes é devido. Comece pelos que vieram por último e termine com os primeiros.'
pt.R: No fim da tarde, o dono da vinha falou com o homem que cuidava dos seus trabalhadores. Ele disse: 'Chame os trabalhadores e pague a eles. Comece pelas pessoas que eu contratei por último e termine com as que contratei primeiro.'

am.L: በመሸም ጊዜ የወይን ቦታው ጌታ መጋቢውን እንዲህ ይለዋል፦ “ሠራተኞቹን ጥራና ከኋለኞቹ ጀምረህ እስከ ፊተኞቹ ድረስ ደመወዛቸውን ክፈላቸው።”
am.B: በመሸ ጊዜ የወይን ቦታው ባለቤት የሥራ ኃላፊውን “ሠራተኞቹን ጠርተህ ደመወዛቸውን ክፈላቸው። በመጨረሻ ከተቀጠሩት ጀምረህ በመጀመሪያ በተቀጠሩት ጨርስ” አለው።
am.R: ምሽት በሆነ ጊዜ የወይን ቦታው ባለቤት ሠራተኞቹን የሚቆጣጠረውን ሰው ጠራው። እንዲህም አለው፦ “ሠራተኞቹን ጥራና ክፈላቸው። በመጨረሻ ከቀጠርኳቸው ጀምር፤ በመጀመሪያ በቀጠርኳቸው ጨርስ።”

ru.L: Когда же наступил вечер, говорит господин виноградника управляющему своему: “Позови работников и отдай им плату, начав с последних до первых.”
ru.B: Когда наступил вечер, хозяин виноградника сказал своему управляющему: “Позови работников и выдай им плату. Начни с тех, кого наняли последними, и закончи первыми.”
ru.R: Когда наступил вечер, хозяин виноградника позвал человека, который отвечал за его работников. Он сказал: “Позови работников и заплати им. Начни с тех, кого я нанял последними, и закончи теми, кого я нанял первыми.”

hi.L: और जब शाम हुई, तो दाख की बारी का स्वामी अपने प्रबंधक से कहता है, 'मज़दूरों को बुलाओ और उन्हें मज़दूरी चुका दो, पिछलों से आरंभ करके पहलों तक।'
hi.B: जब शाम हुई, तो दाख की बारी के मालिक ने अपने प्रबंधक से कहा, 'मज़दूरों को बुलाओ और उन्हें उनकी मज़दूरी दे दो। जो सबसे बाद में आए, उनसे शुरू करना और जो सबसे पहले आए, उन पर ख़त्म करना।'
hi.R: जब शाम हुई, तो बाग़ के मालिक ने उस आदमी से बात की जो उसके मज़दूरों की देखरेख करता था। उसने कहा, 'मज़दूरों को बुलाओ और उन्हें मज़दूरी दे दो। जिन्हें मैंने सबसे बाद में रखा था, उनसे शुरू करना, और जिन्हें सबसे पहले रखा था, उन पर ख़त्म करना।'

uk.L: Коли ж настав вечір, каже пан виноградника своєму управителеві: “Поклич робітників і віддай їм плату, почавши від останніх аж до перших.”
uk.B: Коли настав вечір, власник виноградника сказав своєму управителеві: “Поклич робітників і дай їм плату. Почни з тих, кого найняли останніми, і закінчи першими.”
uk.R: Коли настав вечір, власник виноградника звернувся до чоловіка, який наглядав за його робітниками. Він сказав: “Поклич робітників і заплати їм. Почни з тих, кого я найняв останніми, і закінчи тими, кого я найняв першими.”

ja.L: さて夕方になると、ぶどう園の主人は自分の管理人に言う。『労働者たちを呼んで、最後の者たちから始めて最初の者たちまで、彼らに賃金を払いなさい。』
ja.B: 夕方になると、ぶどう園の持ち主は管理人に言った。『労働者たちを呼んで、賃金を払ってやりなさい。最後に来た者たちから始めて、最初に来た者たちで終わるように。』
ja.R: 夕方になると、ぶどう園の持ち主は、働く人たちを取りしきる人に言った。『働いた人たちを呼んで、賃金を払いなさい。最後に雇った人たちから始めて、最初に雇った人たちを最後にしなさい。』

decisions.choice: evening: the end of the working day, when wages were paid
decisions.reason: The law told employers to pay a hired worker before sunset on the day of the work (Leviticus 19:13; Deuteronomy 24:14-15).

decisions.choice: master: the owner of the vineyard
decisions.reason: The word can mean "lord". In the story it is the owner, though the story points to God.

decisions.choice: foreman: a manager put in charge of the estate's business
decisions.reason: The word is used of a steward or manager who acted for the owner.

decisions.choice: from the last to the first: the order lets the first see what the last receive
decisions.reason: Because the last are paid first, those hired first see their pay and expect more (20:10). The order also acts out the saying in 20:16.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: owner
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use a word that says who he is in the story.

decisions.choice: encargado
decisions.reason: The Greek word is a manager put in charge of an estate's business (meaning decision m3). "Mayordomo" today suggests a butler in a house, and "capataz" only an overseer of the work.

decisions.choice: son intendant
decisions.reason: The man manages the estate's business (m3); "intendant" is the French word for a steward of an estate, where "contremaître" is a factory foreman.

decisions.choice: "người quản lý" (L, B); "người trông coi những người làm công" (R) for the foreman
decisions.reason: The steward who manages the workers; Readable says what he does.

decisions.choice: "주인" for kyrios; "관리인" (L, B), "일꾼들을 맡아 관리하는 사람" (R)
decisions.reason: The master is the owner of the vineyard (meaning decision); "주님" is kept for God and Jesus. The foreman managed the estate's business; "청지기" is the older church word.

decisions.choice: [주어라]
decisions.reason: Korean needs the verb again at the end of "from the last to the first"; Literal brackets it.

decisions.choice: o administrador
decisions.reason: The word is used of a steward who manages an estate for its owner (m3). A Brazilian "capataz" oversees labourers in the field, which is narrower, and "mordomo" is now a butler. Readable describes him, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "መጋቢ" (L); "የሥራ ኃላፊ" (B); "ሠራተኞቹን የሚቆጣጠረው ሰው" (R)
decisions.reason: "መጋቢ" is the steward who runs a household's business, the closest single word; Balanced and Readable use the plain words for the man in charge of the workers.

decisions.choice: "хозяин виноградника" (B, R); "господин виноградника" (L)
decisions.reason: "Kyrios" here is the owner of the vineyard; Literal keeps "господин", Balanced and Readable say "хозяин", the everyday word for an owner and employer.

decisions.choice: "主人" (L); "持ち主" (B, R); "管理人" (L, B); "働く人たちを取りしきる人" (R)
decisions.reason: The master is the owner of the vineyard (m2); Literal keeps the word used of masters in parables, and Balanced and Readable say who he is in the story, as the English does. The foreman managed the estate for him (m3); Readable says what he did.

source.text: καὶ ἐλθόντες οἱ περὶ τὴν ἑνδεκάτην ὥραν ἔλαβον ἀνὰ δηνάριον.

records.literal_gloss: And having come those about the eleventh hour they received each a denarius.

en.L: And those [hired] about the eleventh hour came, and they received a denarius each.
en.B: Those hired around five o'clock came, and each of them was given {{units:a full day's wage|a denarius}}.
en.R: The workers who started at five o'clock came first. Each of them got {{units:a full day's pay|a denarius}}.

es.L: Y llegaron los [contratados] hacia la hora undécima y recibieron un denario cada uno.
es.B: Llegaron los que habían sido contratados hacia las cinco de la tarde, y cada uno recibió {{units:el salario de un día entero|un denario}}.
es.R: Los trabajadores que habían empezado a las cinco de la tarde llegaron primero. Cada uno recibió {{units:la paga de un día completo|un denario}}.

fr.L: Et ceux [embauchés] vers la onzième heure sont venus et ont reçu chacun un denier.
fr.B: Ceux qui avaient été embauchés vers dix-sept heures sont venus, et chacun a reçu {{units:le salaire d’une journée entière|un denier}}.
fr.R: Les ouvriers qui avaient commencé à cinq heures de l’après-midi sont venus les premiers. Chacun d’eux a reçu {{units:la paie d’une journée entière|un denier}}.

sw.L: Na walipofika wale [walioajiriwa] yapata saa kumi na moja, kila mmoja alipokea dinari moja.
sw.B: Wale walioajiriwa karibu saa kumi na moja walikuja, na kila mmoja wao akapewa {{units:mshahara wa siku nzima|dinari moja}}.
sw.R: Wafanyakazi walioanza kazi saa kumi na moja jioni walikuja kwanza. Kila mmoja wao alipata {{units:malipo ya siku nzima|dinari moja}}.

vi.L: Và những người [được mướn] khoảng giờ thứ mười một đến, mỗi người nhận một đơ-ni-ê.
vi.B: Những người được mướn lúc khoảng năm giờ chiều đến, và mỗi người được trả {{units:đủ tiền công một ngày|một đơ-ni-ê}}.
vi.R: Những người bắt đầu làm lúc năm giờ chiều đến trước. Mỗi người nhận được {{units:đủ tiền công một ngày|một đơ-ni-ê}}.

ko.L: 그리고 열한째 시쯤에 [고용된] 사람들이 와서 한 데나리온씩 받았다.
ko.B: 오후 다섯 시쯤에 고용된 사람들이 와서 저마다 {{units:하루 품삯|한 데나리온}}을 받았다.
ko.R: 오후 다섯 시쯤에 일을 시작한 일꾼들이 먼저 왔다. 그들은 저마다 {{units:하루 일한 품삯|한 데나리온}}을 받았다.

pt.L: E, vindo os [contratados] por volta da hora décima primeira, receberam um denário cada um.
pt.B: Chegaram os que tinham sido contratados por volta das cinco da tarde, e cada um recebeu {{units:o salário de um dia inteiro|um denário}}.
pt.R: Os trabalhadores que começaram às cinco horas da tarde vieram primeiro. Cada um deles recebeu {{units:o pagamento de um dia inteiro|um denário}}.

am.L: በአሥራ አንደኛውም ሰዓት ገደማ [የተቀጠሩት] መጥተው እያንዳንዳቸው አንድ ዲናር ተቀበሉ።
am.B: ከቀኑ አሥራ አንድ ሰዓት ገደማ የተቀጠሩት መጡ፤ እያንዳንዳቸውም {{units:የሙሉ ቀን ደመወዝ|አንድ ዲናር}} ተሰጣቸው።
am.R: ከቀኑ አሥራ አንድ ሰዓት ሥራ የጀመሩት ሠራተኞች መጀመሪያ መጡ። እያንዳንዳቸውም {{units:የሙሉ ቀን ክፍያ|አንድ ዲናር}} ተቀበሉ።

ru.L: И придя, [нанятые] около одиннадцатого часа получили по денарию.
ru.B: Пришли те, кого наняли около пяти часов, и каждый получил {{units:плату за целый день|денарий}}.
ru.R: Первыми пришли работники, которые начали в пять часов. Каждый из них получил {{units:плату за целый день|один денарий}}.

hi.L: और जो ग्यारहवें घंटे के लगभग [लगाए गए थे], वे आए और उन्हें एक-एक दीनार मिला।
hi.B: जो लगभग पाँच बजे लगाए गए थे, वे आए, और उनमें से हर एक को {{units:पूरे दिन की मज़दूरी मिली|एक दीनार मिला}}।
hi.R: जिन मज़दूरों ने शाम पाँच बजे काम शुरू किया था, वे पहले आए। उनमें से हर एक को {{units:पूरे दिन की मज़दूरी मिली|एक दीनार मिला}}।

uk.L: І прийшли ті, [найняті] близько одинадцятої години, й отримали по динарію.
uk.B: Прийшли ті, кого найняли близько пʼятої, і кожен із них отримав {{units:повну денну плату|динарій}}.
uk.R: Першими прийшли робітники, які почали о пʼятій. Кожен із них отримав {{units:повну плату за день|динарій}}.

ja.L: そして、第十一の時ごろ[に雇われた]者たちが来て、一デナリオンずつ受け取った。
ja.B: 午後五時ごろに雇われた者たちが来ると、一人一人に{{units:まる一日分の賃金|一デナリオン}}が支払われた。
ja.R: 夕方の五時から働いた人たちが、最初に来た。その一人一人が{{units:まる一日分の賃金|一デナリオン}}をもらった。

decisions.choice: a denarius each: a whole day's wage for one hour's work
decisions.reason: The last workers receive what the first agreed to for a full day. This is the surprise of the story.

decisions.choice: {{units:a full day's wage|a denarius}}
decisions.reason: As in 20:2, the coin's worth is the default and the coin itself the alternative.

decisions.choice: five o'clock
decisions.reason: The day was counted from sunrise, about six in the morning, in twelve hours (John 11:9). Balanced and Readable give the time as a modern reader tells it; Literal keeps the hour as the Greek counts it.

decisions.choice: [고용된]
decisions.reason: The Greek says "those about the eleventh hour"; Korean needs a verb for the phrase, which Literal brackets.

decisions.choice: cinco da tarde
decisions.reason: The English Balanced and Readable say "five o'clock" alone; Portuguese adds "da tarde", since Brazilians tell the hour on a twelve-hour clock and "às cinco" alone could be read as early morning.

source.text: καὶ ἐλθόντες οἱ πρῶτοι ἐνόμισαν ὅτι πλεῖον λήμψονται· καὶ ἔλαβον τὸ ἀνὰ δηνάριον καὶ αὐτοί.

records.literal_gloss: And having come the first thought that more they will receive; and they received each a denarius also themselves.

en.L: And when the first came, they thought that they would receive more; and they themselves also received a denarius each.
en.B: So when the first ones came, they expected to get more. But they too were each paid {{units:a day's wage|a denarius}}.
en.R: Then the workers who had been hired first came. They thought they would get more money. But each of them also got {{units:one day's pay|a denarius}}.

es.L: Y cuando llegaron los primeros, creyeron que recibirían más; y también ellos mismos recibieron un denario cada uno.
es.B: Así que, cuando llegaron los primeros, esperaban cobrar más. Pero también a ellos se les pagó {{units:el salario de un día|un denario}} a cada uno.
es.R: Después llegaron los trabajadores que habían sido contratados primero. Pensaban que iban a recibir más dinero. Pero cada uno de ellos también recibió {{units:la paga de un día|un denario}}.

fr.L: Et quand les premiers sont venus, ils ont pensé qu’ils recevraient davantage ; et ils ont reçu, eux aussi, un denier chacun.
fr.B: Quand les premiers sont venus à leur tour, ils s’attendaient à recevoir davantage. Mais eux aussi ont reçu chacun {{units:le salaire d’une journée|un denier}}.
fr.R: Ensuite, les ouvriers qui avaient été engagés en premier sont venus. Ils pensaient qu’ils allaient recevoir plus d’argent. Mais chacun d’eux a reçu, lui aussi, {{units:la paie d’une journée|un denier}}.

sw.L: Na wale wa kwanza walipofika, walifikiri watapata zaidi; nao wenyewe pia wakapata dinari moja kila mmoja.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo wale wa kwanza walipofika, walitarajia kupata zaidi. Lakini nao pia kila mmoja alilipwa {{units:mshahara wa siku moja|dinari moja}}.
sw.R: Kisha wakaja wafanyakazi walioajiriwa kwanza. Walifikiri watapata fedha zaidi. Lakini kila mmoja wao naye alipata {{units:malipo ya siku moja|dinari moja}}.

vi.L: Và khi những người đầu tiên đến, họ tưởng rằng mình sẽ nhận được nhiều hơn; nhưng chính họ cũng nhận mỗi người một đơ-ni-ê.
vi.B: Vì vậy, khi những người được mướn trước nhất đến, họ tưởng mình sẽ được nhiều hơn. Nhưng họ cũng chỉ được trả mỗi người {{units:tiền công một ngày|một đơ-ni-ê}}.
vi.R: Rồi những người được mướn trước hết đến. Họ nghĩ mình sẽ được trả nhiều tiền hơn. Nhưng mỗi người trong họ cũng chỉ nhận được {{units:tiền công một ngày|một đơ-ni-ê}}.

ko.L: 그리고 처음 사람들이 와서, 자기들은 더 많이 받을 것이라고 생각했다. 그러나 그들도 한 데나리온씩 받았다.
ko.B: 그래서 맨 먼저 온 사람들은 더 많이 받을 것이라고 생각했다. 그러나 그들도 {{units:하루 품삯|한 데나리온}}씩 받았다.
ko.R: 그다음에 맨 처음 고용된 일꾼들이 왔다. 그들은 돈을 더 많이 받을 거라고 생각했다. 그러나 그들도 {{units:하루 일한 품삯|한 데나리온}}씩 받았다.

pt.L: E, vindo os primeiros, pensaram que receberiam mais; e também eles receberam um denário cada um.
pt.B: Quando chegaram os primeiros, eles esperavam receber mais. Mas também eles receberam, cada um, {{units:o salário de um dia|um denário}}.
pt.R: Depois vieram os trabalhadores que tinham sido contratados primeiro. Eles pensaram que iam ganhar mais dinheiro. Mas cada um deles também recebeu {{units:o pagamento de um dia|um denário}}.

am.L: ፊተኞቹም መጥተው አብልጠው እንደሚቀበሉ አሰቡ፤ እነርሱም ደግሞ እያንዳንዳቸው አንድ ዲናር ተቀበሉ።
am.B: ስለዚህ የመጀመሪያዎቹ በመጡ ጊዜ ብዙ እንደሚያገኙ ጠበቁ። ነገር ግን እነርሱም እያንዳንዳቸው {{units:የአንድ ቀን ደመወዝ|አንድ ዲናር}} ተከፈላቸው።
am.R: ከዚያም በመጀመሪያ የተቀጠሩት ሠራተኞች መጡ። ብዙ ገንዘብ እንደሚያገኙ አሰቡ። ነገር ግን እነርሱም እያንዳንዳቸው {{units:የአንድ ቀን ክፍያ|አንድ ዲናር}} አገኙ።

ru.L: И придя, первые подумали, что получат больше; и получили по денарию и они сами.
ru.B: Поэтому, когда пришли первые, они ожидали получить больше. Но и им дали каждому по {{units:дневной плате|денарию}}.
ru.R: Потом пришли работники, которых наняли первыми. Они думали, что получат больше денег. Но каждый из них тоже получил {{units:плату за один день|один денарий}}.

hi.L: और जब पहले वाले आए, तो उन्होंने सोचा कि उन्हें अधिक मिलेगा; और उन्हें भी एक-एक दीनार ही मिला।
hi.B: इसलिए जब पहले वाले आए, तो उन्हें उम्मीद थी कि उन्हें अधिक मिलेगा। पर उनमें से भी हर एक को {{units:एक दिन की मज़दूरी ही मिली|एक दीनार ही मिला}}।
hi.R: फिर वे मज़दूर आए जिन्हें सबसे पहले काम पर रखा गया था। उन्होंने सोचा कि उन्हें ज़्यादा पैसे मिलेंगे। पर उनमें से भी हर एक को {{units:एक ही दिन की मज़दूरी मिली|एक ही दीनार मिला}}।

uk.L: Прийшли й перші й думали, що отримають більше; але й вони самі отримали по динарію.
uk.B: Тож коли прийшли перші, вони сподівалися отримати більше. Але й вони отримали кожен {{units:денну плату|по динарію}}.
uk.R: Потім прийшли робітники, яких найняли першими. Вони думали, що отримають більше грошей. Але й кожен із них отримав {{units:плату за один день|динарій}}.

ja.L: そして最初の者たちが来たとき、彼らはもっと多く受け取るだろうと思った。しかし、彼ら自身もまた一デナリオンずつ受け取った。
ja.B: そこで、最初の者たちが来たとき、もっと多くもらえるだろうと思った。しかし、彼らも{{units:一日分の賃金|一デナリオン}}ずつであった。
ja.R: それから、最初に雇われた人たちが来た。この人たちは、もっとたくさんもらえるだろうと思った。ところが、この人たちも{{units:一日分の賃金|一デナリオン}}ずつだった。

decisions.choice: they also: the same pay as the last, and what they had agreed to
decisions.reason: They receive exactly the wage they agreed to in 20:2. What troubles them is that the last receive it too.

decisions.choice: {{units:a day's wage|a denarius}}
decisions.reason: As in 20:2.

source.text: λαβόντες δὲ ἐγόγγυζον κατὰ τοῦ οἰκοδεσπότου λέγοντες· Οὗτοι οἱ ἔσχατοι μίαν ὥραν ἐποίησαν, καὶ ἴσους αὐτοὺς ἡμῖν ἐποίησας τοῖς βαστάσασι τὸ βάρος τῆς ἡμέρας καὶ τὸν καύσωνα.

records.literal_gloss: Having received now they were grumbling against the master of the house \v 12 saying, These the last one hour worked, and equal them to us you have made, those having borne the burden of the day and the scorching heat.

en.L: And having received [it], they were grumbling against the master of the house, \v 12 saying, 'These last ones worked one hour, and you have made them equal to us who have borne the burden of the day and the scorching heat.'
en.B: When they were paid, they began to grumble at the landowner. \v 12 'The ones who came last put in a single hour,' they said, 'and you have treated them the same as us, though we carried the load of the whole day in the burning heat.'
en.R: When they got their pay, they started to complain about the owner. \v 12 They said, 'These people who came last worked for only one hour. But you paid them the same as us! We worked hard all day long in the hot sun.'

es.L: Y habiendo recibido [la paga], murmuraban contra el señor de la casa, \v 12 diciendo: “Estos, los últimos, trabajaron una hora, y los has igualado a nosotros, los que hemos cargado con el peso del día y con el calor abrasador”.
es.B: Al cobrar, empezaron a murmurar contra el propietario. \v 12 “Estos que llegaron los últimos han trabajado apenas una hora —decían—, y los has tratado igual que a nosotros, que hemos aguantado la carga de toda la jornada bajo un calor abrasador”.
es.R: Cuando recibieron su paga, comenzaron a quejarse del dueño. \v 12 Le dijeron: “Estos que llegaron al final trabajaron solo una hora. ¡Pero les has pagado lo mismo que a nosotros! Nosotros trabajamos duro todo el día bajo el sol ardiente”.

fr.L: Et l’ayant reçu, ils murmuraient contre le maître de maison, \v 12 disant : “Ces derniers-là ont travaillé une heure, et tu les as rendus égaux à nous, qui avons porté le poids du jour et la chaleur brûlante.”
fr.B: En le recevant, ils se sont mis à murmurer contre le propriétaire : \v 12 “Ces derniers venus n’ont fait qu’une heure, ont-ils dit, et tu les as traités comme nous, qui avons porté le poids de toute la journée sous une chaleur brûlante !”
fr.R: Quand ils ont reçu leur paie, ils se sont plaints du propriétaire. \v 12 Ils ont dit : “Ces gens arrivés les derniers ont travaillé seulement une heure. Et tu les as payés autant que nous ! Nous, nous avons travaillé dur toute la journée, sous un soleil brûlant.”

sw.L: Na walipoipokea, walikuwa wakimnung'unikia mwenye nyumba, \v 12 wakisema, 'Hawa wa mwisho walifanya kazi saa moja, nawe umewafanya walingane nasi, sisi tuliobeba uzito wa siku na joto kali.'
sw.B: Walipolipwa, wakaanza kumnung'unikia mwenye shamba, \v 12 wakisema, 'Hawa waliokuja mwisho wamefanya kazi saa moja tu, lakini umewatendea sawa na sisi, ingawa tumebeba mzigo wa kazi ya siku nzima katika joto kali.'
sw.R: Walipopata malipo yao, wakaanza kulalamika juu ya mwenye shamba. \v 12 Wakasema, 'Hawa waliokuja mwisho walifanya kazi saa moja tu. Lakini umewalipa sawa na sisi! Sisi tumefanya kazi ngumu siku nzima katika jua kali.'

vi.L: Nhận [tiền] rồi, họ lằm bằm với chủ nhà \v 12 rằng: 'Những người sau cùng này chỉ làm một giờ, mà ông lại coi họ ngang bằng với chúng tôi, là những người đã chịu gánh nặng của cả ngày và cái nắng thiêu đốt.'
vi.B: Khi lãnh tiền, họ bắt đầu lằm bằm với chủ. \v 12 Họ nói: 'Những người đến sau cùng chỉ làm có một giờ, mà ông lại đối xử với họ ngang bằng với chúng tôi, là những người đã làm lụng vất vả suốt cả ngày dưới cái nắng thiêu đốt.'
vi.R: Khi nhận tiền công, họ bắt đầu phàn nàn với ông chủ. \v 12 Họ nói: 'Những người đến sau cùng chỉ làm có một giờ. Nhưng ông lại trả cho họ bằng chúng tôi! Chúng tôi đã làm việc cực nhọc suốt cả ngày dưới trời nắng nóng.'

ko.L: 그리고 그들은 받고 나서 집주인에게 불평하며 \v 12 말했다. '이 마지막 사람들은 한 시간 일했는데, 주인께서는 그들을 하루의 짐과 뙤약볕을 견딘 저희와 똑같게 만드셨습니다.'
ko.B: 그들은 품삯을 받고 나서 집주인에게 불평했다. \v 12 '맨 나중에 온 이 사람들은 겨우 한 시간 일했습니다. 그런데 주인님께서는 온종일 뙤약볕 아래서 힘들게 일한 저희와 그들을 똑같이 대하셨습니다.'
ko.R: 그들은 품삯을 받고 나서 주인에게 불평했다. \v 12 '맨 나중에 온 이 사람들은 한 시간밖에 일하지 않았습니다. 그런데 주인님께서는 저희와 똑같이 주셨습니다! 저희는 하루 종일 뜨거운 햇볕 아래서 힘들게 일했습니다.'

pt.L: E, tendo recebido, murmuravam contra o senhor da casa, \v 12 dizendo: 'Estes últimos trabalharam uma hora, e o senhor os fez iguais a nós, que suportamos o peso do dia e o calor escaldante.'
pt.B: Ao receberem o pagamento, começaram a resmungar contra o proprietário. \v 12 'Esses que chegaram por último trabalharam uma hora só', disseram eles, 'e o senhor os tratou do mesmo modo que a nós, que carregamos o peso do dia inteiro debaixo do calor escaldante.'
pt.R: Quando receberam o pagamento, começaram a reclamar do dono. \v 12 Eles disseram: 'Essas pessoas que chegaram por último trabalharam só uma hora. Mas o senhor pagou a elas o mesmo que a nós! Nós trabalhamos duro o dia inteiro debaixo do sol quente.'

am.L: ተቀብለውም በቤቱ ጌታ ላይ ያጉረመርሙ ነበር፤ \v 12 እንዲህም እያሉ፦ “እነዚህ ኋለኞች አንድ ሰዓት ሠሩ፤ የቀኑን ሸክምና ሐሩሩን ከተሸከምነው ከእኛ ጋር እኩል አደረግሃቸው።”
am.B: ደመወዛቸውንም በተቀበሉ ጊዜ በባለቤቱ ላይ ማጉረምረም ጀመሩ። \v 12 “እነዚህ በመጨረሻ የመጡት አንድ ሰዓት ብቻ ሠሩ” አሉ፤ “እኛ ግን ቀኑን ሙሉ በሚያቃጥል ሙቀት ሸክሙን ተሸክመን ሳለ ከእኛ ጋር እኩል አደረግሃቸው።”
am.R: ክፍያቸውን በተቀበሉ ጊዜ በባለቤቱ ላይ ማማረር ጀመሩ። \v 12 እንዲህም አሉ፦ “እነዚህ በመጨረሻ የመጡት ሰዎች የሠሩት አንድ ሰዓት ብቻ ነው። አንተ ግን ልክ እንደ እኛ ከፈልካቸው! እኛ በኃይለኛው ፀሐይ ቀኑን ሙሉ በብርቱ ሠርተናል።”

ru.L: Получив же, они роптали на хозяина дома, \v 12 говоря: “Эти последние один час поработали, и ты сравнял их с нами, перенёсшими тяжесть дня и зной.”
ru.B: Получив плату, они стали ворчать на хозяина. \v 12 “Эти последние проработали всего один час”, — говорили они, — “а ты приравнял их к нам, хотя мы несли тяжесть целого дня под палящим зноем.”
ru.R: Получив деньги, они начали жаловаться на хозяина. \v 12 Они говорили: “Эти люди пришли последними и работали только один час. А ты заплатил им столько же, сколько нам! Мы тяжело работали весь день под жарким солнцем.”

hi.L: और [उसे] पाकर वे घर के स्वामी के विरुद्ध कुड़कुड़ाने लगे, \v 12 और कहने लगे, 'इन पिछलों ने एक ही घंटा काम किया, और आपने इन्हें हमारे बराबर कर दिया है, जिन्होंने दिन का बोझ और झुलसाती गर्मी सही है।'
hi.B: जब उन्हें मज़दूरी मिली, तो वे ज़मींदार पर कुड़कुड़ाने लगे। \v 12 'जो सबसे बाद में आए, उन्होंने बस एक घंटा काम किया,' उन्होंने कहा, 'और आपने उन्हें हमारे बराबर कर दिया, जबकि हमने सारे दिन का बोझ उठाया और कड़ी धूप सही।'
hi.R: जब उन्हें पैसे मिले, तो वे मालिक की शिकायत करने लगे। \v 12 उन्होंने कहा, 'जो लोग सबसे बाद में आए, उन्होंने सिर्फ़ एक घंटा काम किया। पर आपने उन्हें उतना ही दिया जितना हमें! हमने तो सारा दिन तेज़ धूप में कड़ी मेहनत की।'

uk.L: Отримавши ж, вони нарікали на господаря, \v 12 кажучи: “Ці останні працювали одну годину, і ти зрівняв їх з нами, які винесли тягар дня і спеку.”
uk.B: Отримавши плату, вони почали нарікати на господаря. \v 12 “Ті, що прийшли останніми, пропрацювали лише одну годину”, — казали вони, — “а ти прирівняв їх до нас, хоч ми несли тягар цілого дня під пекучим сонцем.”
uk.R: Коли вони отримали свою плату, то почали скаржитися на власника. \v 12 Вони казали: “Ці люди, які прийшли останніми, працювали лише одну годину. А ти заплатив їм стільки ж, скільки нам! А ми тяжко працювали цілий день на гарячому сонці.”

ja.L: そして受け取ると、彼らは家の主人に対して不平を言い続けて、\v 12 言った。『この最後の者たちは一時間働いただけです。それなのに、あなたは彼らを、一日の重荷と焼けつく暑さに耐えたわたしたちと同じにしました。』
ja.B: 賃金を受け取ると、彼らは地主に向かって不平を言いだした。\v 12 『最後に来た者たちは、たった一時間しか働いていません』と彼らは言った。『それなのに、あなたは彼らを、焼けつく暑さの中で一日中重荷を負ったわたしたちと同じに扱いました。』
ja.R: 賃金をもらうと、その人たちは持ち主に文句を言い始めた。\v 12 『最後に来た人たちは、たった一時間しか働いていません。それなのに、わたしたちと同じだけ払うなんて！わたしたちは一日中、暑い日差しの中で一生懸命働いたのですよ。』

decisions.choice: were grumbling: kept muttering complaints
decisions.reason: The verb pictures low, resentful complaint, and the tense shows that it went on. Israel grumbled against God in the wilderness in the same way (Exodus 16:7-8).

decisions.choice: you have made them equal to us: the complaint is equal treatment
decisions.reason: They do not say they were paid less than agreed. They object that the others were treated as their equals.

decisions.choice: the scorching heat: the burning heat of the day, perhaps the hot east wind
decisions.reason: The word is used of burning heat and of the hot wind from the desert (Jonah 4:8; James 1:11).

decisions.choice: only
decisions.reason: Readable adds "only" to give the tone of the complaint, which the Greek gives by setting one hour against the whole day.

decisions.choice: murmuraient (L); se sont mis à murmurer (B)
decisions.reason: French "murmurer contre" is the established word for grumbling against someone (m1); Readable says "se plaindre", as the English "complain".

decisions.choice: "lằm bằm" (L, B); "phàn nàn" (R) for grumbling
decisions.reason: "lằm bằm" is the low, resentful complaining the Greek word describes; Readable uses the everyday word.

decisions.choice: The workers complain to the owner in 합쇼체, calling him "주인" (L), "주인님" (B, R) for "you"
decisions.reason: Even in their grumbling they speak to their employer deferentially; Korean says "you" to a superior with his title. The complaint is equal treatment (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: "뙤약볕" (L, B); "뜨거운 햇볕" (R)
decisions.reason: The scorching heat of the day (meaning decision, which notes it may be the hot east wind); "뙤약볕" is the Korean word for burning midday sun.

decisions.choice: o senhor
decisions.reason: Hired laborers speak up to the landowner who employs them, so they say "o senhor", as Brazilians address an employer or superior (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 4); "você" would sound rude to a Brazilian ear. The owner answers one of them with "você" (20:13-15).

decisions.choice: "ሐሩር" (the scorching heat)
decisions.reason: "ሐሩር" names the burning heat of the day, as the Greek word does; "ትኩሳት" means a fever. Balanced and Readable say it plainly ("የሚያቃጥል ሙቀት", "ኃይለኛው ፀሐይ").

decisions.choice: "ты" from the workers to the owner
decisions.reason: As the style guide sets out (section 4), ordinary people say "ты" to one person, and respect is carried by the words used; the owner also stands for God in the story, whom Russian addresses as "ты".

decisions.choice: the workers say "आप" to the landowner; he says "तुम" to them (20:13-15)
decisions.reason: Day laborers speak to the man who hires them with respect, even while complaining, as the style guide asks of servants to a master. The landowner stands for God in the story, but the address follows the scene.

decisions.choice: "不平を言い続けて" (L); "不平を言いだした" (B); "文句を言い始めた" (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is low, resentful complaint that went on (m1). Literal keeps the continuing tense; Balanced and Readable give its start, as the English does. The workers still speak politely to the man who pays them, but their words are resentful.

source.text: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς ἑνὶ αὐτῶν εἶπεν· Ἑταῖρε, οὐκ ἀδικῶ σε· οὐχὶ δηναρίου συνεφώνησάς μοι;

records.literal_gloss: And answering to one of them he said, Friend, not I do wrong you; not for a denarius did you agree with me?

en.L: But he answered one of them and said, 'Friend, I am not doing you wrong. Did you not agree with me for a denarius?
en.B: But he replied to one of them, 'Friend, I have done you no wrong. Was it not for {{units:a day's wage|a denarius}} that you made your agreement with me?
en.R: The owner answered one of them, 'Friend, I am not cheating you. You agreed to work for {{units:one day's pay|a denarius}}, did you not?

es.L: Pero él respondió a uno de ellos y dijo: “Amigo, no te estoy haciendo injusticia. ¿No te pusiste de acuerdo conmigo por un denario?
es.B: Pero él le contestó a uno de ellos: “Amigo, no te he hecho ninguna injusticia. ¿No quedaste conmigo en {{units:el salario de un día|un denario}}?
es.R: El dueño le contestó a uno de ellos: “Amigo, no te estoy engañando. Tú aceptaste trabajar por {{units:la paga de un día|un denario}}, ¿no es cierto?

fr.L: Mais lui, répondant à l’un d’eux, a dit : “Ami, je ne te fais pas de tort ; ne t’es-tu pas mis d’accord avec moi pour un denier ?
fr.B: Mais il a répondu à l’un d’eux : “Mon ami, je ne t’ai fait aucun tort. N’est-ce pas pour {{units:le salaire d’une journée|un denier}} que tu t’es mis d’accord avec moi ?
fr.R: Le propriétaire a répondu à l’un d’eux : “Mon ami, je ne te vole pas. Tu as accepté de travailler pour {{units:la paie d’une journée|un denier}}, n’est-ce pas ?

sw.L: Lakini yeye akamjibu mmoja wao, akasema, 'Rafiki, sikutendei isivyo haki. Je, hukukubaliana nami kwa dinari moja?
sw.B: Lakini yeye alimjibu mmoja wao, 'Rafiki yangu, sijakutendea isivyo haki. Je, hukukubali nikulipe {{units:mshahara wa siku moja|dinari moja}}?
sw.R: Mwenye shamba akamjibu mmoja wao, 'Rafiki, sikupunji. Wewe ulikubali kufanya kazi kwa {{units:malipo ya siku moja|dinari moja}}, sivyo?

vi.L: Nhưng ông đáp lời một người trong họ và nói: 'Này bạn, tôi không làm sai với anh; chẳng phải anh đã thỏa thuận với tôi một đơ-ni-ê sao?
vi.B: Ông trả lời một người trong bọn họ: 'Này anh bạn, tôi không làm gì sai với anh cả. Chẳng phải anh đã thỏa thuận với tôi {{units:tiền công một ngày|một đơ-ni-ê}} sao?
vi.R: Ông chủ trả lời một người trong họ: 'Này anh bạn, tôi không lừa anh đâu. Anh đã đồng ý làm việc để nhận {{units:tiền công một ngày|một đơ-ni-ê}}, phải không?

ko.L: 그러나 그가 그들 가운데 한 사람에게 대답하여 말했다. '친구여, 나는 너에게 잘못하고 있지 않다. 너는 한 데나리온으로 나와 합의하지 않았느냐?
ko.B: 주인이 그들 가운데 한 사람에게 대답했다. '친구여, 나는 너에게 잘못한 것이 없다. 너는 나와 {{units:하루 품삯|한 데나리온}}으로 약속하지 않았느냐?
ko.R: 주인이 그들 가운데 한 사람에게 대답했다. '친구여, 나는 너를 속이지 않았다. 너는 {{units:하루 일한 품삯|한 데나리온}}을 받고 일하기로 나와 약속하지 않았느냐?

pt.L: Mas ele, respondendo a um deles, disse: 'Amigo, não lhe faço injustiça; não foi por um denário que você combinou comigo?
pt.B: Mas ele respondeu a um deles: 'Amigo, eu não fui injusto com você. Não foi {{units:pelo salário de um dia|por um denário}} que você fez o acordo comigo?
pt.R: O dono respondeu a um deles: 'Amigo, eu não estou enganando você. Você combinou trabalhar {{units:pelo pagamento de um dia|por um denário}}, não foi?

am.L: እርሱ ግን ከእነርሱ ለአንዱ መልሶ እንዲህ አለ፦ “ወዳጄ ሆይ፣ አልበድልህም፤ ከእኔ ጋር በአንድ ዲናር አልተስማማህምን?
am.B: እርሱ ግን ከእነርሱ ለአንዱ እንዲህ ሲል መለሰለት፦ “ወዳጄ፣ ምንም አልበደልሁህም። ከእኔ ጋር የተስማማኸው {{units:በአንድ ቀን ደመወዝ|በአንድ ዲናር}} አልነበረምን?
am.R: ባለቤቱም ከእነርሱ ለአንዱ እንዲህ ሲል መለሰለት፦ “ወዳጄ፣ እኔ አላታለልሁህም። {{units:የአንድ ቀን ክፍያ|አንድ ዲናር}} ልትቀበል ተስማምተህ ነበር፤ አይደለም እንዴ?

ru.L: Он же, ответив одному из них, сказал: “Друг, я не обижаю тебя. Не о денарии ли ты договорился со мной?
ru.B: Но он ответил одному из них: “Друг, я не поступил с тобой несправедливо. Разве ты не за {{units:дневную плату|денарий}} договорился со мной?
ru.R: Хозяин ответил одному из них: “Друг, я тебя не обманываю. Ты ведь согласился работать за {{units:плату за один день|один денарий}}, правда?

hi.L: पर उसने उनमें से एक को उत्तर देते हुए कहा, 'मित्र, मैं तुम्हारे साथ अन्याय नहीं कर रहा। क्या तुमने मुझसे एक दीनार पर सहमति नहीं की थी?
hi.B: पर उसने उनमें से एक को उत्तर दिया, 'मित्र, मैंने तुम्हारे साथ कोई अन्याय नहीं किया। क्या तुमने मुझसे {{units:एक दिन की मज़दूरी|एक दीनार}} पर ही समझौता नहीं किया था?
hi.R: मालिक ने उनमें से एक को जवाब दिया, 'दोस्त, मैं तुम्हें ठग नहीं रहा। तुमने {{units:एक दिन की मज़दूरी|एक दीनार}} पर काम करना मान लिया था, है न?

uk.L: А він, відповідаючи одному з них, сказав: “Друже, я тебе не кривджу. Хіба ти не за динарій домовився зі мною?
uk.B: Але він відповів одному з них: “Друже, я не вчинив тобі кривди. Хіба не за {{units:денну плату|динарій}} ти зі мною домовився?
uk.R: Власник відповів одному з них: “Друже, я тебе не обманюю. Ти ж погодився працювати за {{units:плату за один день|динарій}}, правда?

ja.L: すると彼は、そのうちの一人に答えて言った。『友よ、わたしはあなたに不正をしてはいない。あなたはわたしと一デナリオンで合意したではないか？
ja.B: しかし地主はその一人に答えた。『友よ、わたしはあなたに何も不当なことはしていない。あなたは{{units:一日分の賃金|一デナリオン}}で、わたしと約束したではないか？
ja.R: 持ち主はその一人に答えた。『友よ、わたしはあなたをだましてはいない。あなたは{{units:一日分の賃金|一デナリオン}}で働くと、わたしと約束したではないか？

decisions.choice: Friend: a polite address to someone who is in the wrong
decisions.reason: Matthew uses this word only when the one spoken to is at fault (22:12; 26:50). It is courteous but cool.

decisions.choice: I am not doing you wrong: I am not being unjust to you
decisions.reason: The owner kept the agreement exactly. Fairness is not the question; generosity is (20:15).

decisions.choice: {{units:a day's wage|a denarius}}
decisions.reason: As in 20:2.

decisions.choice: the owner's words run on to 20:15
decisions.reason: The owner's answer runs through three sentences, so the inner quotation opens here and closes at the end of 20:15.

decisions.choice: Amigo
decisions.reason: A polite address to someone who is in the wrong (meaning decision m1). Spanish "amigo" carries that same cool courtesy when used to correct someone.

decisions.choice: Ami (L); Mon ami (B, R); "tu" to the one worker
decisions.reason: The address is polite but cool, said to someone in the wrong (m1); "Mon ami" carries that tone in French. The owner speaks to one man, so "tu", as the style guide sets.

decisions.choice: sikupunji (I am not short-changing you)
decisions.reason: The English Readable says "cheating". "Kupunja" is to pay someone less than is owed, which is what the worker complains of; "kudanganya" would mean lying to him.

decisions.choice: "Này bạn" (L); "Này anh bạn" (B, R) for "Friend"
decisions.reason: A polite but cool address; Vietnamese adds "anh" in Balanced and Readable, as speech to a laborer would.

decisions.choice: "친구여" for hetaire
decisions.reason: A polite address to someone who is in the wrong (meaning decision); "친구여" keeps the courtesy while the owner speaks in 해라체. His words run on to 20:15, so the inner quotation stays open.

decisions.choice: {{units:pelo salário de um dia|por um denário}}
alternatives: por {{units:o salário de um dia|um denário}}
decisions.reason: The preposition contracts with the article of the default ("pelo") but not with the alternative ("por um"), so it goes inside both options.

decisions.choice: "ወዳጄ" (Friend)
decisions.reason: "ወዳጄ" is a courteous address that can carry a note of reproof, as the Greek word does here; "ጓደኛዬ" would sound like real companionship.
A polite address that keeps a little distance (meaning decision m1); Readable uses the everyday word.

decisions.choice: "友よ" at every level; 『 opens here and 』 closes at the end of 20:15
decisions.reason: The address is courteous but cool, used in Matthew to someone in the wrong (m1); "友よ" keeps that distance at each level. The owner's answer runs over three records, so the inner bracket stays open, as in the English.

source.text: ἆρον τὸ σὸν καὶ ὕπαγε· θέλω δὲ τούτῳ τῷ ἐσχάτῳ δοῦναι ὡς καὶ σοί·

records.literal_gloss: Take what [is] yours and go; I desire now to this the last to give as also to you;

en.L: Take what [is] yours and go. But I want to give to this last [one] as also to you.
en.B: Take what is yours and be on your way. It is my choice to give this last worker just what I gave you.
en.R: Take your money and go home. I have decided to pay the worker who came last the same as you.

decisions.choice: an evil eye: envy, a grudging spirit
decisions.reason: In Hebrew an "evil eye" means a grudging, envious attitude (Deuteronomy 15:9; Proverbs 28:22). Jesus uses the same phrase in 6:23. Here it is the look of someone who resents another person's good fortune.

decisions.choice: good: generous, kind
decisions.reason: The word means good, and here it is the goodness of a generous giver. The play is between the worker's evil eye and the owner's good heart.

decisions.choice: do you look on my generosity with an evil eye
alternatives: are you envious because I am generous
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the evil eye, as in 6:23, and joins it to what the man looks on.

decisions.choice: angry and jealous
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom.

decisions.choice: me miras con malos ojos
decisions.reason: "Mirar con malos ojos" is a living Spanish idiom for looking on someone with resentment, close to the Greek "evil eye" for envy (meaning decision m1), so Balanced can keep the eye.

decisions.choice: unanionea kijicho
decisions.reason: Swahili "kijicho" (literally a little eye) is envy, the same picture as the Greek "evil eye" (meaning decision m1), so Balanced keeps the eye in a natural idiom.

decisions.choice: "mắt anh xấu" (L); "con mắt ganh tị" (B); "giận và ganh tị" (R)
decisions.reason: An "evil eye" is a jealous, grudging look; Literal keeps the picture, Balanced and Readable say what it means.

decisions.choice: "네 눈이 악하냐" (L); "시기하는 눈으로 보다" (B); "샘이 나다" (R); "선하다" (L), "너그럽게 베풀다" (B), "친절하게 대하다" (R)
decisions.reason: An evil eye is envy, a grudging spirit, and good here is generous (meaning decisions); Literal keeps the picture, which Korean readers would not take as envy, so Balanced and Readable say it.

decisions.choice: "ተናደሃል፣ ቀንተሃልም" (R) for the evil eye
decisions.reason: In Amharic "ክፉ ዓይን" can call up the belief in a harmful gaze; Literal and Balanced keep the image, and Readable names what the idiom means here, envy, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "смотришь недобрым глазом"
decisions.reason: In Russian "дурной глаз" is the evil eye of a curse; "смотреть недобрым глазом" keeps the image while meaning envy and ill will.

decisions.choice: "あなたの目は悪い" (L); "悪い目で見る" (B); "腹を立ててねたんでいる" (R); "善い" (L), "気前よくする" (B), "親切にする" (R)
decisions.reason: The evil eye is envy, a grudging look at another's good fortune (m1), and "good" is the goodness of a generous giver (m2). Literal and Balanced keep the eye of 6:23 ("目が悪ければ"); Readable says what it means, as the English Readable does.
